prose_updates.tldr: On the explicit first-difference region \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}=\{0<\alpha,\beta,\gamma\leq1\}\), one bounded local cross-pair estimator attains the optimizer-defined KBRW three-term pointwise-CATE benchmark under only a fixed positive two-sided covariate-density band.  Both deterministic branches use the same screened ratio at distance \(\delta=h_n^*(k_n^*)^{-1/d}\); direct causal numerator algebra and complete diagonal/shared-index variance accounting give the bound without a Gram matrix, nuisance estimate, density estimate, or logarithmic loss.  The validity region includes the nonempty open outside-bank set \(U=\{0<\alpha<\beta<\gamma<1\}\), but no containment of the full banked region or validity above first-difference smoothness is claimed.

project_justification.gap: The KBRW benchmark is known, but the supplied literature receipts do not prove that a localized same-sample M"obius estimator attains it under a merely bounded nonsmooth design density.  They also do not transfer variance-contrast identities to the causal numerator/denominator ratio.  The unresolved higher-order route is therefore not used as a premise.
project_justification.niche: On the explicitly restricted positive-band class and \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\), close pairs provide exactly the local mass \(h^{2d}/k\) needed for an order-one product remainder.  Overlap supplies a deterministic population denominator margin, while direct overlap-graph counting controls both diagonal and shared-index variance terms.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives the explicit close-pair set, screened denominator, ratio, and bounded fallback; proves its bias, occupancy, screen probability, and variance equation by equation; exhibits the outside-bank open set \(U\); and stitches the two deterministic labels into one total estimator attaining \(r_n^*\) without density estimation or logarithmic loss.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The proved estimator does not estimate the propensity, either outcome regression, or the covariate density.  Their known H"older indices select the deterministic optimizer and guarantee the order-one pair-bias bound; no smoothness or estimation rate is imposed on the density.

prose_updates.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) supply the three-term pointwise-CATE objective used here as the benchmark; their theorem class is not claimed to contain or be contained in the present fixed positive-band class.  Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020) and Dobriban, Mukherjee, Robins, and Wang (2026) motivate close-pair contrasts for noncausal variance problems, but neither source proves the causal two-point numerator/denominator identity or the overlap-graph bounds used here.  Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2017) and Liu, Li, Gu, and Liu (2026) concern empirical-Gram or stabilized HOIF constructions; no projection, spectral, or M"obius theorem from those papers is imported into this proof.  The present result instead derives the first-difference cross-pair analysis directly.
prose_updates.interpretation: The optimizer still determines \(h_n^*\) and \(k_n^*\), but the labels \(G_n\) and \(P_n\) no longer select different statistical algorithms on the proved region: both invoke the same total cross-pair map.  A close pair makes the propensity and control-regression increments multiply, producing \(\delta^{\alpha+\beta}\), while localization contributes \(h^\gamma\).  The number and overlap pattern of pairs produce exactly \(N^{-1/2}+\sqrt{k}/N\), which is dominated by the benchmark variance term.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The proof is restricted to \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\) because first differences yield the asserted H"older increment bounds only through order one.  It does not establish that this region contains all of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{bank}}\).  A singular Gram is irrelevant because the proved estimator uses no Gram matrix, and no support-hole construction is used as a converse.  \textbf{Conditional extension bracket.}  Extension beyond \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\) would require an explicitly specified higher-order random-design contrast or localized M"obius estimator together with a proved uniform \(L^\infty\) projection bound, causal numerator/denominator expansion, spectral-screen probability, and complete collision/Hoeffding accounting.  None of those conditions is asserted here or imported from the current literature receipts.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Identification is given by the frozen CATE identification lemma.  The proved advance is an explicit, density-free, no-logarithmic-loss upper bound for one total local cross-pair estimator on \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\), including the outside-bank open set \(U\).  The paper does not claim an arbitrary-smoothness HOIF theorem, a minimal higher-order projected-tuple correction above order one, containment of the full banked region, a positive-band minimax converse, adaptive unknown-smoothness inference, or a density-induced slowdown.
